extraction.name: CommonCatalog
extraction.description: A dataset of roughly 70 million open-licensed Creative-Commons images curated from YFCC100M and paired with high-quality synthetic captions generated using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model, used to train the CommonCanvas family of text-to-image diffusion models.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan; A. Feder Cooper; Jasmine Collins; Landan Seguin; Austin Jacobson; Mihir Patel; Jonathan Frankle; Cory Stephenson; Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.citeAs: Gokaslan, Aaron, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, and Volodymyr Kuleshov. "CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images." arXiv:2310.16825, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors curated Creative-Commons-licensed images for CommonCatalog by beginning with the YFCC100M dataset, which contains 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs linking to the original data. They re-scraped the images from Flickr based on the IDs in the YFCC100M metadata to obtain high-resolution images, excluded images with non-derivative licenses, and divided the remaining images into commercial and non-commercial subsets. They then generated synthetic captions for the curated CC images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper explicitly discusses data incompleteness: almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a high-quality text-to-image model. It also notes that CC images rarely have alt-text captions, and those that do often only include the image title or a URL.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source was Creative-Commons images sourced from the YFCC100M dataset and re-scraped from Flickr using the Flickr IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. The dataset contains open-licensed CC images, with CommonCatalog-C containing commercially usable images and CommonCatalog-NC additionally including non-commercial images. Synthetic captions were generated with a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors re-scraped YFCC100M images from Flickr to obtain higher-resolution versions, excluded images with non-derivative licenses, split the remaining data into commercial and non-commercial subsets, and generated synthetic captions for all curated images using BLIP-2.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For caption generation, all images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels because captioning images at native resolution would be very expensive. At diffusion model training time, all images remained in their native resolution.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset labels are synthetic captions generated automatically using the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B image captioning model. The authors compared several captioning models and selected BLIP-2 based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO. They captioned all YFCC100M Creative-Commons images using this model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors compared several captioning models and chose BLIP-2 based on qualitative analysis and MS COCO performance. They report that BLIP-2 captions were often qualitatively more descriptive than corresponding LAION-2B alt-text captions, while citing prior work showing BLIP-2 captions are higher quality in terms of CLIP Score but have reduced caption diversity. They also observed reduced diversity of n-grams in their synthetic captions, visible through a decrease in unique trigrams.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that they release the CommonCatalog dataset of CC images and synthetic captions, along with trained CommonCanvas models and code, and that the commercial and non-commercial datasets are released on HuggingFace with associated data cards. They also release BLIP-2 captions for the non-derivative CC images not used for training as an evaluation set.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper discusses generation involving faces, celebrities, and public figures, and notes that the model can generate some noteworthy public figures. It also mentions prompts suggestive of iconic characters and examples involving individual people.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as a possible path forward for training high-quality text-to-image models using only open-licensed Creative-Commons data, motivated by copyright concerns and reproducibility issues with web-scraped datasets like LAION. It also shows that CommonCanvas is less likely than SD2 to generate recognizable copyrighted characters from suggestive prompts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note domain shift between MS COCO captions and web-scraped conceptual captions, and state that CLIP-FID likely favors SD2 because CLIP is trained on a similar style of text as LAION. They also report that synthetic captions have reduced diversity of n-grams compared to ground-truth captions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that CommonCanvas underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings. It notes the importance of large-scale human-generated caption data, and that transitioning to synthetic captions introduces performance challenges. It also states that the YFCC100M data is about a decade old, so its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. Additionally, although trained on Creative-Commons images, the model can still produce content resembling iconic characters under adversarial prompts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training text-to-image diffusion models in the CommonCanvas family. The authors release commercial and non-commercial versions of the dataset, and also release captions for excluded non-derivative images as an evaluation set. The paper positions the dataset as an open alternative to LAION for training high-quality text-to-image models.
